summary: Ash utilisation, coal-handling and related industrial services, with a wind-equipment business through Venwind Refex. Historic activities need separate, dated reading.
description: Refex Industries helps industrial customers handle materials and operating needs around power plants. Ash is a by-product of burning coal; handling and finding approved uses for it is a different business from generating electricity. The wind-equipment subsidiary introduces a separate manufacturing and execution model.
money: Contracts can earn service revenue and material-related sales under their own terms. Equipment, transport, labour, site operations, working capital and collection determine what remains. Wind equipment has its own order, manufacturing, installation and warranty cycle.
customers: Thermal power plants and industrial customers, users of ash where appropriate, and customers of the wind-equipment business. Who pays for transport or material depends on the individual contract.
drivers: Contract volumes and terms, plant activity, material handling, route efficiency, permitted utilisation, receivables and the execution and funding of new wind-equipment activity.
productNote: These offerings describe the ash, coal and wind businesses in the cited materials. Power trading, refrigerant gases and green mobility were classified as discontinued in the financial disclosure for the quarter and nine months ended December 2025. That dated accounting classification does not by itself establish their subsequent legal ownership or completion of disposal; do not treat an older group website menu as a current company catalogue.

groups.title: Ash management and utilisation
groups.examples: Fly ash, pond ash and movement to appropriate utilisation sites.
groups.explanation: Handling, transportation and end-use arrangements form an operating chain. A reuse claim needs the relevant material suitability, permissions and actual destination.

groups.title: Coal and site services
groups.examples: Supply and handling, coal-yard management and related operating services.
groups.explanation: Material volume, equipment availability, staffing and contract responsibilities affect execution. This does not mean the company owns every plant it serves.

groups.title: Wind equipment through a subsidiary
groups.explanation: Manufacturing, customer acceptance, service and warranties differ from recurring handling work. Read the subsidiary’s actual stage, orders and group funding separately.

basics.title: Fly ash and pond ash are related but different materials
basics.text: Fly ash is collected from a combustion process; ash stored in ponds needs its own reclamation and handling arrangements. Transport and suitability for an end use can change the economics.

basics.title: A group brand is not a reporting boundary
basics.text: Other businesses using the Refex name are not automatically operations or assets of Refex Industries. Use its consolidated notes and entity list to establish the scope.

steps.title: Agree the contract
steps.text: Identify volumes, service duties, transport responsibility and payment terms.

steps.title: Mobilise and execute
steps.text: Arrange sites, people, equipment and permitted material movement.

steps.title: Confirm and bill
steps.text: Measure completed work or supplied goods and obtain the required customer approvals.

steps.title: Collect and reinvest
steps.text: Recover receivables while paying operating costs and funding equipment or expansion.

specifics.title: Logistics can decide contract economics
specifics.text: A short, reliable route and suitable destination differ from a long or disrupted one. More tonnes handled do not guarantee a better margin when mobilisation, fuel and maintenance also rise.

specifics.title: Continuing and discontinued results must stay separate
specifics.text: The cited interim accounts classified several activities as discontinued. This is an accounting presentation with a specified period, not proof that all legal transfers had already finished or that the old activity never existed.

specifics.title: Wind activity changes the execution questions
specifics.text: Order conversion, technical qualification, production, acceptance and warranty obligations need reading. A project announcement is not the same as completed delivery or collected customer cash.

watch: What is inside the reported company now?
A historic website menu can outlive a reporting change.

Read continuing and discontinued operations, subsidiaries and disposal notes for the exact period. Track subsequent announcements before asserting current ownership, and keep the listed company distinct from the wider Refex group.
Work performed may remain in receivables.

Compare operating cash flow with earnings, customer balances and collection commentary. Examine approval, billing and contract terms rather than assuming every tonne handled immediately produces cash.
Do the ash routes and utilisation arrangements work?
Destination and distance affect delivery costs and compliance.
Read customer duties, permitted end uses, transport responsibilities and actual operating progress. Distinguish a contract award from mobilised capacity and completed utilisation.
Are equipment and customers becoming concentrated?
A contract or plant interruption can affect utilisation.
Read customer concentration, renewal conditions, equipment commitments and plant exposure. Ask whether assets and people can move to another contract if an important customer’s activity slows.
Is the wind business progressing beyond announcements?
Manufacturing commitments can require cash before acceptance.

Read capacity commissioning, firm orders, customer advances, delivery and service obligations. Separate subsidiary activity from the parent’s established handling operations, and investigate the funding and guarantees involved.
risks: Customer approvals, disputes or slow payment can delay cash.
Fuel, maintenance, utilisation and operating interruptions affect costs.
Material handling requires appropriate permissions and safe execution.
Manufacturing ramp-up, guarantees, disposals and group transactions can change risk and comparability.
context: Use the disclosure date to resolve conflicting descriptions

The interim financial filing is the stronger source for its reported accounting scope when a marketing menu still lists older businesses. Read any later filing before carrying that conclusion forward to a different reporting date.
quiz: Does an ash-handling contract mean Refex owns the customer’s electricity-generation business?
No. It may provide material and operating services to that plant. Ownership, responsibilities, revenue and risks depend on the disclosed company and contract.

financialNotes.title: Do not combine different operating scopes
financialNotes.text: The cited filing classifies power trading, refrigerant gases and green mobility as discontinued for the quarter and nine months ended December 2025. A fresh final-year breakdown has not been added here. Use the signed reporting period’s continuing/discontinued reconciliation rather than combining a historic total with a newer business description.

financialNotes.title: Read operating cash and subsidiary obligations
financialNotes.text: Contract receivables, equipment investment, wind-business funding and guarantees can require cash despite accounting earnings. A group total does not establish a separate margin for ash, coal or wind without a matching segment disclosure.
